record.paper_title: Properly Coloured Cycles and Paths: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Determine the specific constant s(2) in the asymptotic formula d(n,2) = s(2) log_2 n (1 + o(1)), where d(n,2) is the minimum integer k such that every 2-edge-coloured graph on n vertices and minimum monochromatic degree at least k contains a properly coloured cycle.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.2. [15] There is a function s(c) dependent only on c such that d(n, c) = s(c) log2 n(1 + o(1)).
In particular, it would be interesting to determine s(2).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite simple graph on n vertices, and let c: E(G) → {1, 2} be a 2-edge-coloring of G. The monochromatic degree of a vertex v in color i is the number of edges of color i incident to v, and the minimum monochromatic degree of (G, c) is the minimum, over all vertices v and both colors i ∈ {1, 2}, of these monochromatic degrees. A cycle in G is properly coloured if every two consecutive edges along the cycle have different colors.

Define d(n, 2) to be the minimum integer k such that every graph G on n vertices, equipped with any 2-edge-coloring whose minimum monochromatic degree is at least k, contains a properly coloured cycle.

It is known (conjecturally) that there exists a constant s(2) > 0 such that
   d(n, 2) = s(2) · log_2 n · (1 + o(1))   as n → ∞.

Determine the exact value of the constant s(2).
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches for the asymptotic constant s(2) governing the minimum monochromatic degree threshold d(n,2) for forcing a properly coloured cycle in 2-edge-coloured graphs returned no resolution. Related literature treats monochromatic-cycle partitions and rainbow cycles, but no source provides the value of s(2). The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Monochromatic paths and cycles in 2-edge-coloured graphs with large minimum degree
status_evidence.snippet: Studies monochromatic structures under minimum-degree conditions in 2-edge-coloured graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on minimum-degree conditions in 2-edge-coloured graphs does not determine the constant s(2) for properly coloured cycles.

status_evidence.title: Properly colored cycles in edge-colored complete graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates the existence of properly coloured cycles in edge-coloured complete graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on properly coloured cycles concerns colour-count thresholds rather than the asymptotic constant s(2) in the logarithmic minimum-degree threshold.
